name: Eswatini
summary_text: Eswatini is dangerous for trans visitors. Common law criminalises same-sex intimacy; trans people have no access to LGR and limited healthcare; the absolute monarchy punishes dissent harshly (sedition laws; activists assassinated, per BTI 2024); LGBT people face documented discrimination. Eswatini Pride has proceeded annually since 2018 under heavy conditions — a small space of visibility.

sources.title: Eswatini | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): common law criminalises consensual same-sex intimacy; no legal gender recognition and limited gender-affirming healthcare; intersex people lack safeguards; in April 2022 the High Court rejected ESGM's bid for registration, but in June 2023 the Supreme Court declared the Registrar's decision void; the Ministry of Commerce still refuses registration, claiming the NGO's name and objectives 'seek to offend against customary principles'.

sources.title: Eswatini: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House
sources.claim_summary: Freedom House 2024 for Eswatini: 'Not Free' (17/100) - an absolute monarchy; political dissent harshly punished; discrimination against women and LGBT+ people among the human-rights problems.
BTI 2024 Country Report Eswatini (Bertelsmann): the last absolute monarchy in Africa - the King and Queen Mother hold veto powers over all branches of government; governance and human-rights context.

sources.title: Eswatini - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Eswatini: official assessment - sodomy laws (common law) remain; significant societal stigma; no legal protections for LGBT persons.

Swazi Media Commentary (Dec 2018): a church welcoming LGBTIQ people reopened in Coates Valley; Rock of Hope's Melusi Simelane welcomed it while noting religious hate speech; a Gender Links report described a meeting where 20+ pastors called LGBTI behaviour 'demonic' and refused to let gay people 'flaunt' themselves.

sources.title: History made as first eSwatini Pride declared a "perfect" success - MambaOnline - LGBTQ South Africa online
sources.claim_summary: Mambaonline (July 2018): history made as the first eSwatini Pride was declared a 'perfect' success - more than 2,000 people attended in Mbabane, with a police-escorted march around Prince of Wales Stadium; organiser Melusi Simelane of Rock of Hope was 'beyond thrilled'.

sources.title: Eswatini government refuses to register LGBTI group - MambaOnline - LGBTQ South Africa online
sources.claim_summary: Mambaonline (July 2019): Eswatini's registrar of companies refused to register Eswatini Sexual and Gender Minorities (ESGM), calling its objectives a 'negative mindset' - other groups had to include 'acceptable' health/HIV aims to register; ESGM's first objective is to advance LGBT rights.
